citation.authors: Bulengo-Ransby SM, Griffiths CE, Kimbrough-Green CK, Finkel LJ et al

record.population: 54 Black adults with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation who completed the study
record.design: Randomised, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, 40 weeks; tretinoin 0.1% cream (a prescription medicine) on face or arms against vehicle cream
record.finding: Facial lesions in the tretinoin group were significantly lighter than vehicle (P<0.001). Colorimetry showed 40% lightening of lesions against 18% with vehicle (P=0.05). Improvement began after about 4 weeks. Retinoid dermatitis developed in 12 of 24 tretinoin-treated people (50%) but eased with time. Tretinoin lightened normal skin slightly.
record.note: 1993; relatively small; prescription in the UK. Mentioned as evidence that a class of treatment (prescription retinoids) has been tested in Black people, not as a dose.
